on: The lemonade table opens for the afternoon beneath its striped awning.
off: The jug rests by the lane, and the striped awning keeps its shade.
idle: The lemonade table is open; the lane is quiet.
front: Fig Jr.’s lemonade stand. Ask Fig Jr. for a job and you can pour lemonade here for tips.
left: Somebody turns from the table, leaving the awning to its shade.

receipt.title: Lemonade Tally
receipt.line: The jug waits at the table while Hall Street keeps its sun.
receipt.none: The jug kept cool company beneath the striped awning.
receipt.capped: Glasses went down the lane; the day’s tips are already spent.
receipt.best: A {drink} glass went down the lane with ice clicking.

perfect: Ice ticks in a bright glass as it goes down the lane.
A lemon slice catches the sun above the glass.
The straw leaves with a glass cold enough for Hall Street.
Someone takes the glass before the ice can settle.
fine: The glass goes out cool, with a lemon doing its best.
The ice reaches the lane before it can melt.
A straw leans cheerfully from the glass.
The glass heads down the lane with its ice still arguing.
wrong: The glass stays on the table, lemon and ice in a muddle.
No glass goes down the lane; the lemons keep the secret.
The ice settles back into a glass nobody takes.
This glass remains at the table, bright but unclaimed.
